name: Humanist photography
summary: A warm and tender form of documentary photography from France. It shows the everyday life of ordinary people in streets and bistros. It joins sympathy with wit, and it hopes for a world of mutual care.

philosophy.core_thesis: Ordinary people share a human nature, and a photograph of everyday life can show their dignity, their humour and their need for each other.
design_principles: Photograph ordinary life in the street, the bistro, the market and the working-class district, and not news events.
Use available light and a small camera, a 35mm lens or a waist-level Rolleiflex, so that people do not notice you.
Stand 1.5 to 4m away, so that the face and the setting share the frame.
Wait for a gesture of tenderness or wit: a child at play, a couple, a shared joke.
Print in black and white with deep mid-tones and a soft contrast.
Work in series for the picture essay, and publish it in a magazine or a book.
anti_patterns: Cold, distant views of people as types
Harsh flash that flattens the face
Heavy blur or grain that hides the person
Pictures of news events or battles with no human warmth

composition.framing: Loose and readable; the frame holds the person and the room or street around them.
composition.viewpoint: Eye or waist height, handheld, 1.5 to 4m from the subject.
composition.geometry: Gentle diagonals, doorways and window light; a small human drama sits inside the setting.
composition.subject_placement: Off centre, with the gesture or the gaze of the person in a pocket of light.

principles.rule: Give 1 human gesture as the point of the picture and let the setting support it.
Put 2 or 3 planes in the frame: a foreground detail at 1.5m, the person at 3m and the street beyond.
Balance the frame by a second figure or a shop sign within 0.8 to 1.25 of the visual weight.
Put the main figure within 0.05 of 0.33 or 0.67 of the width.

light.quality: Available light: soft daylight, a café window or the street lamp at dusk.
light.direction: Side light from windows and low sun; gentle backlight.
light.time_of_day: Morning or late afternoon; early evening in town

lens_and_camera.focus: Set by scale or on the ground glass; the subject stays sharp with softly blurred surroundings.

colour_and_grade.treatment: Black and white with rich mid-tones and a gentle S-curve; the tone is warm and human.
grade_recipe: Convert to monochrome with a yellow-orange filter mix (R 45, G 45, B 10).
Set the black point at 2% and the white point at 96%.
Apply +15% midtone contrast with a soft S-curve.
Dodge the faces by +0.3 stop and burn the corners by −0.3 stop.
Add film grain, amount 15%, size 30%, as for ISO 400 film.
Keep the full frame; crop by no more than 5%.
colour_and_grade.grain: ISO 400 film: fine and even, visible at A4

subject_and_staging.staging: Little or none. The photographer waits, and may speak to the person first.
subject_and_staging.direction: People are at ease; they ignore the camera or give a short, natural smile.

workflow: Develop in a standard developer at ISO 400, with no push.
Make a contact sheet of the whole series and choose the frames that tell a story.
Print on grade 2 to 3 paper with soft burning at the edges.
Order the prints as a picture essay for a magazine or a book.
post_processing.output: A warm black and white 8×10 in print, or a series of 6 to 12 prints for a picture essay.

positive: children at play in the street

canonical_works.work: Le baiser de l'hôtel de ville

emotion.target_response: Warm recognition: the viewer feels fellowship with an ordinary person and smiles with them.

use_cases: image prompts for warm street scenes
avoid_when: The brief needs a harsh, raw or edgy mood.
The brief needs a news event or a staged glossy ideal.

modifiers.how: Push ISO 3200, shoot at 1/30s handheld, tilt the frame and print with crushed blacks.
Move to a tripod and a 150mm lens at f/32, with even light and a frontal view; photograph the person as a type.
